paragraphs.excerpt: The fundamental data structure in neural networks is the layer, to which
paragraphs.what_it_says: The layer is the fundamental data structure in neural networks. It is a data processing module taking one or more tensors in and outputting one or more tensors. Some layers are stateless, but most have state: weights, one or more tensors learned by SGD, which together contain the network's knowledge.
paragraphs.what_it_means: A layer = a function plus (usually) parameters. A Dense layer has a kernel W and bias b. A Flatten or ReLU-activation layer has no weights and just transforms its input. Training is the process of adjusting the weight tensors, so what the model 'knows' is stored in those numbers.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Everything else in Keras is built around this abstraction (p.117): models are graphs of layers.
paragraphs.technical_idea: A layer with weights computes $y = f(x; \theta)$, where $\theta$ are the weights updated by gradient descent. A stateless layer computes $y = f(x)$. (Notation ours.)

concepts.name: Keras backend configuration
concepts.definition: The mechanism that selects which low-level framework Keras runs on: the KERAS_BACKEND environment variable or the "backend" field of ~/.keras/keras.json.
concepts.intuition: It is a switch that is read once, when Keras starts up.
concepts.technical: Valid values are "jax", "tensorflow" and "torch". It must be set before import keras. The default is tensorflow.
concepts.significance: Every Keras example depends on it. The authors recommend JAX for performance.
concepts.misconception: "pytorch" is not a valid backend name; use "torch".

concepts.name: Layer
concepts.definition: A data processing module that takes one or more tensors as input and outputs one or more tensors, usually with state (weights).
concepts.intuition: It is a LEGO brick of deep learning (p.117): a reusable transformation you clip together with others.
concepts.technical: Most layers hold weight tensors learned with SGD. Some are stateless. In Keras, weights are created in build() and computation is defined in call() (p.117).
concepts.significance: It is the central abstraction of Keras; models are assembled from layers.
concepts.example: A Dense layer with weights W and b computes activation(matmul(input, W) + b).
concepts.misconception: Not every layer has trainable weights; some are stateless.

concepts.name: floatx and epsilon settings
concepts.definition: Global Keras defaults for floating-point precision (float32) and a small 'numerical fuzzing factor' (1e-07).
concepts.intuition: epsilon is a tiny number added in places where dividing by zero or taking log(0) could happen.
concepts.technical: Beyond the book: epsilon is used e.g. to clip probabilities in cross-entropy losses and in some normalization or optimizer formulas. floatx sets the dtype of newly created weights.
concepts.significance: The book says both should typically not be changed.
concepts.misconception: Changing floatx to float16 is not the right way to do mixed-precision training. Keras has a dedicated mixed-precision policy for that (beyond the book).

deeper.title: What 'channels_last' means
deeper.body: Beyond the book (chapter 8 covers it): an image batch can be laid out as `(samples, height, width, channels)`, which is **channels_last**, or `(samples, channels, height, width)`, which is **channels_first**. Keras defaults to channels_last. Convolution and pooling layers read this setting to know which axis holds the colour channels.

deeper.title: Why the order of the two lines matters
deeper.body:
1. `import keras` runs Keras's initialization code.
2. That code looks up `KERAS_BACKEND`, falling back to keras.json and then to TensorFlow.
3. It imports the chosen framework and binds Keras's ops to it.
4. Python caches imported modules, so a second `import keras` does not rerun step 2.

This is why the book says the snippet must imperatively go before the first import. (The mechanism is our explanation.)

deeper.title: Layers as knowledge containers
deeper.body: Think of a layer as a machine on an assembly line with adjustable dials. Data flows through and is transformed. The dial settings are the weights. Training turns the dials, so the final dial positions are what the network has 'learned', which is the book's 'knowledge'.

questions.question: Which backend string selects PyTorch?
questions.explanation: The NOTE says to use "torch" because the package is named torch. "pytorch" is explicitly invalid, and the other two are not valid names either.

questions.question: Why must os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "jax" appear before import keras?
questions.answer: Keras reads the backend setting when it is first imported. Setting it afterwards doesn't change the already-loaded backend.
questions.explanation: The page says it must imperatively go before the first import keras, and the callout says 'Only then should you import Keras.'

questions.question: In the default keras.json, which field does the book say you should change to switch backends?
questions.explanation: The callout says to change "tensorflow" to "jax" or "torch" in the backend field. floatx and epsilon should typically not be changed, and image_data_format is the image layout (chapter 8).

questions.question: Which backend do the authors recommend if you have no preference, and why?
questions.answer: JAX, because it is usually the most performant.
questions.explanation: Stated in the 'Now, you may ask…' paragraph.

questions.question: Define a layer as the book does and explain where a network's 'knowledge' lives.
questions.answer: A layer is a data processing module taking one or more tensors in and outputting one or more tensors. Most layers have state, their weights, which are learned by SGD. Together the weights contain the network's knowledge.

questions.question: What does "image_data_format": "channels_last" describe?
options: The default image layout, with channels on the last axis
That only the last channel is used
The image file format to save
questions.answer: The default image layout, with channels on the last axis
questions.explanation: The callout calls it the default image layout (chapter 8). It is about axis order in tensors, not RGB ordering, channel selection or file formats.
